articles.title: Create a WhatsApp template and get it approved
articles.description: Create a WhatsApp message template in TopEdge AI, choose the right category, add variables and buttons, submit it to Meta and fix a rejection.
articles.h1: How to create a WhatsApp template
articles.lead: Write a message once, send it to Meta for approval, then use it in any journey or campaign.

faqs.question: How long does Meta take to approve a template?
faqs.answer: Often a few minutes, and usually within a day. Meta does not promise a time. The status in Meta Manager changes to **Approved** on its own.

faqs.question: Why was my template rejected?
faqs.answer: The usual reason is the wrong category: a promotional word such as sale, offer or discount inside a Utility template. Move the promotion to a Marketing template, or remove the word, and submit again.

faqs.question: Can I edit a template after it is approved?
faqs.answer: Editing sends it back to Meta for review, and it cannot send while in review. For a big change, create a new template and switch your journey to it once approved.

blocks.text: Open **Meta Manager** and click **Create Meta template**. Give it a name, choose the category, write the message and press **Submit for review**. You can use it once its status reads **Approved**.

items: WhatsApp is connected: [Connect WhatsApp](/docs/connect-whatsapp).
You know what the message is for: an order update, or a promotion.

blocks.title: Check the blueprints first
blocks.body: The **Blueprints** tab has ready-made sets for order updates and cart recovery, with the image, variables and button already filled in. Start there if one fits.

blocks.text: Create the template

blocks.howToName: Create a WhatsApp message template in TopEdge AI

steps.title: Open Meta Manager
steps.body: In the sidebar click **Meta Manager**, then **Create Meta template** at the top right.
steps.alt: WhatsApp templates list with the Create Meta template button at the top right

steps.title: Name it
steps.body: **Template name** is for you, for example "Order confirmed". **Meta template name** is how Meta files it: lowercase with underscores, like `order_confirmed`.
steps.alt: New WhatsApp template form with template name, Meta template name, category, language, header and body fields

marks.label: Two names: yours, and the one Meta files it under

steps.title: Choose the category
steps.body: Pick **Utility** for messages about an order the customer already placed. Pick **Marketing** for offers, launches and reminders to buy.
steps.note: The form starts on Marketing. Change it for order updates, or Meta charges and reviews the message as marketing.

steps.title: Add a header if you want one
steps.body: Under **Header** choose **Text**, **Image**, **Video** or **Document**. A product image works well for order and cart messages. **None** is fine too.

steps.title: Write the body
steps.body: Type the message. Where a detail changes per customer, click **+ Add variable**. It shows as `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` and is filled with the name, order number or amount when the message sends.

steps.title: Add buttons
steps.body: Under **Buttons** click **Add button**. Use a link button such as "Track order", or quick replies such as "Confirm" and "Cancel".

steps.title: Check the preview and submit
steps.body: The preview on the right is exactly what the customer will see. Press **Submit for review**. To finish later, press **Save draft**.

blocks.text: Check the status

rows: Ready. Pick it in a journey or campaign.
Open it, fix the wording or category, and submit again.

blocks.text: Utility or Marketing?

rows: Order confirmed, shipped, delivered, COD confirmation
Offers, new arrivals, cart reminders with a discount, win-back

blocks.title: One promotional word can reject a Utility template
blocks.body: Words like sale, offer, discount or free gift make Meta treat the message as marketing. Keep order messages about the order.

cases.symptom: The template was rejected
fixes: Remove promotional wording from a Utility template, or change the category to Marketing.
Make sure every variable has ordinary words around it. A message that is only variables is rejected.
Do not start or end the body with a variable.

cases.symptom: The approved template does not appear in a journey
fixes: Press **Sync from Meta** on the step’s template picker.
Check the template was created on the same WhatsApp account that is connected in Settings.
